User.title: User
User.description: Stores user profile information, authentication details (excluding sensitive credentials), and their assigned role within the CongreKids application.

id.description: Unique identifier for the User entity (Firebase Auth UID).

displayName.description: The user's display name, typically from Google Sign-In.

email.description: The user's email address, typically from Google Sign-In.

photoURL.description: URL to the user's profile picture, typically from Google Sign-In.

role.description: The user's role in the application ('parent' or 'admin').

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the user's profile was first created.

Child.title: Child
Child.description: Represents a child associated with a specific parent user for childcare sign-ups in CongreKids.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Child entity.

parentId.description: Reference to the User entity who is the parent of this child. (Relationship: User 1:N Child)

Meeting.title: Meeting
Meeting.description: Defines the details for a specific weekly parent meeting where childcare sign-ups are managed.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Meeting entity.

title.description: The title or name of the meeting.

registrationDeadline.description: The timestamp by which parents must register their children for the meeting. Defaults to Thursday 23:59 before the meeting.

status.description: The current status of the meeting's registration period ('upcoming', 'closed', or 'past').

ageGroups.description: An array of age group definitions for childcare. Each string element is expected to be a JSON serialized object containing 'label' (string), 'minMonths' (number), and 'maxMonths' (number).

createdBy.description: Reference to the User entity (admin) who created this meeting. (Relationship: User 1:N Meeting)

createdAt.description: Timestamp when the meeting record was created.

Registration.title: Registration
Registration.description: Records a parent's sign-up for a specific meeting, detailing which of their children will attend.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Registration entity, typically corresponding to the parent's User ID (uid).

meetingId.description: Reference to the Meeting entity this registration is for. (Relationship: Meeting 1:N Registration)

parentId.description: Reference to the User entity (parent) who made this registration. (Relationship: User 1:N Registration)

parentName.description: Denormalized display name of the parent who registered.

parentEmail.description: Denormalized email address of the parent who registered.

children.description: An array of children registered for this meeting. Each string element is expected to be a JSON serialized object containing 'childId' (string), 'name' (string), 'birthDate' (string, date-time), and 'ageGroupLabel' (string).

registeredAt.description: Timestamp when the registration was first created.

lastUpdatedAt.description: Timestamp when the registration was last updated.

cancelledChildren.description: Optional: An array of children who were initially registered but later cancelled. Each string element is expected to be a JSON serialized object containing 'childId' (string), 'name' (string), and 'cancelledAt' (string, date-time).

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure prioritizes secure, scalable, and debuggable access patterns by adhering to the core design principles, especially Authorization Independence and Query-Aware Security (QAPs). 

1.  **Authorization Independence (Denormalization for Ownership):**
    *   For user-owned subcollections like `/users/{parentId}/children/{childId}`, the `parentId` is explicitly included in the path itself. This allows security rules to directly compare `request.auth.uid` with the `{parentId}` wildcard without needing to perform a `get()` operation on the parent `/users/{parentId}` document. The `Child` entity also stores `parentId` within the document for clarity and redundancy, further bolstering rule simplicity. 
    *   Similarly, for `/meetings/{meetingId}/registrations/{parentId}`, the parent's UID (`parentId`) is both part of the document path and denormalized within the `Registration` document (as `parentId`, `parentName`, `parentEmail`). This enables direct path-based authorization (`request.auth.uid == parentId`) and efficient filtering in queries without requiring `get()` calls to parent collections (like `Meeting` or `User`).
    *   **Note on Global Roles:** The `User` schema provided includes a `role` field. Therefore, authorization for global roles (e.g., checking if `request.auth.uid` is an 'admin') will necessarily rely on a `get(/users/$(request.auth.uid)).data.role == 'admin'` operation in security rules. While this introduces a `get()`, it is a direct consequence of following the provided schema, and it is a controlled `get()` to a known, single document for role verification, minimizing its impact compared to nested `get()` operations for entity ownership.

2.  **Structural Segregation (Homogeneous Security Posture):**
    *   Each collection (e.g., `/users`, `/meetings`, `/users/{parentId}/children`, `/meetings/{meetingId}/registrations`) is designed to contain documents that share a consistent security posture. For example, all documents in `/meetings` are globally readable by authenticated users and writable only by admins. All documents in `/users/{parentId}/children` are owned by the `parentId` in the path. This simplifies security rules significantly by moving complexity from rule logic to the structural organization of data.

3.  **QAPs (Secure List Operations):**
    *   **Parents Listing Their Children:** Parents can securely query and list their own children by accessing `/users/{request.auth.uid}/children`. The rules will ensure `parentId` matches `request.auth.uid`.
    *   **Parents Listing Upcoming Meetings:** All authenticated users can read all documents in `/meetings`, enabling parents to list upcoming meetings without needing specific filtering logic in rules that might be circumvented.
    *   **Parents Listing Their Registrations:** Parents can query for their specific registrations either by accessing `/meetings/{meetingId}/registrations/{request.auth.uid}` directly for a given meeting, or by performing a collection group query on `registrations` filtered by `parentId == request.auth.uid`. The denormalized `parentId` in the `Registration` document is crucial for this efficient and secure querying pattern.
    *   **Admins Listing Data:** Admins, identified by their `role` in the `User` document, will have broad read/write access across all collections, enabling them to list all users, children, meetings, and registrations for oversight and management. This is directly supported by the rule `get(/users/$(request.auth.uid)).data.role == 'admin'` for write operations and list operations.

This design ensures that common access patterns are straightforward to implement with robust security rules, minimizing the risk of data exposure or unauthorized modifications.
